walkthroughs.body_html: Elizabeth's first Parliament passed the Act of Supremacy and Act of Uniformity in April 1559, making her Supreme Governor and imposing the 1552 Prayer Book with minor concessions (the Black Rubric was removed). The 1563 Thirty-Nine Articles defined doctrine moderately Protestant. Marian bishops mostly refused the oath and were replaced; Matthew Parker became Archbishop of Canterbury.

Puritans demanded further reform: the Vestiarian Controversy (1565), Admonitions to Parliament (1572), and presbyterian classis movement of the 1580s. Whitgift's Articles enforced conformity. Catholics faced harsher recusancy fines after 1571. After Regnans in Excelsis (1570), missionary priests faced execution under 1581 and 1585 statutes; Campion was executed in 1581.

Sir John Neale argued in 1953 that Elizabeth wanted a conservative settlement but was forced left by a 'Puritan choir' in the Commons. Norman Jones (1982) reversed this, arguing Elizabeth sought a fully Protestant settlement frustrated by Catholic peers in the Lords. Diarmaid MacCulloch sees the Settlement as broadly Reformed but distinctively English in its retention of episcopacy and liturgical structure.

mcqs.q: What was the Elizabethan Religious Settlement of 1559?
options: Elizabeth reunited England with the Pope to make peace with Spain.
Because the Pope excommunicated him for marrying Anne Boleyn.
A deliberate via media — a Protestant doctrine and English-language prayer book combined with some Catholic-style ceremony — designed to maximise conformity.
Elizabeth made England fully Protestant and banned Catholic worship outright.

mcqs.q: Why did Henry VIII break with Rome?
options: Because he wanted England to become Protestant.
Elizabeth reunited England with the Pope to make peace with Spain.
Because the Pope excommunicated him for marrying Anne Boleyn.
Primarily for an annulment from Catherine of Aragon, but also to seize Church wealth and assert royal supremacy — not for Protestant theological reasons.

mcqs.q: Why was the Spanish Armada defeated in 1588?
options: A combination of English tactics and fireships, poor Spanish planning, and the 'Protestant wind' storms that wrecked the fleet on the return.
Elizabeth reunited England with the Pope to make peace with Spain.
Drake defeated the Armada single-handedly in a great sea battle.
Elizabeth I personally commanded the English fleet at sea.
